players.name: Cameron Boozer
players.verdict: Safest dynasty pick in the 2026 class and lands in MEM where he has the runway to make a rare immediate impact in fantasy. An elite interior scorer and shooter whose strength and rebounding are the foundation of the profile. The youngest prospect in the draft with unbelievable dominance and feel. In his own tier and the clear #1 pick in rookie drafts and top 15 dynasty asset right off the bat.

players.name: Darryn Peterson
players.verdict: Lands in UTA next and will share on-ball duties next to Keyonte George. One of the best perimeter defensive profiles in the class. Expected to develop into a Top 30 category league player.

players.name: AJ Dybantsa
players.verdict: Goes at Pick 1 to the Wizards as expected. Led the nation in scoring as a freshman. First freshman since Trae Young in 2018 to lead the country in PPG. Elite PTS on high volume. A primary advantage creator whose scoring juice is the real thing. Draws fouls at high volume. Dynasty runway is enormous.

players.name: Caleb Wilson
players.verdict: Chicago got themselves a guy that has the potential to be the best in this class! Elite REB, elite STL and elite FG% on volume. One of the best defenders in the class, with the feel and instincts already NBA-ready. Draws fouls at the highest rate in the class. Be patient with him in Year 1 and expect the scoring will come. Season ended early with a broken thumb, but he is now ready to go.

players.name: Kingston Flemings
players.verdict: One of my guys. I like the spot in ATL and think he will show something right away, but this is probably a guy who has a big breakout in Year 2 or 3. The most elite playmaking guard in the 2026 class. Two-way impact built into the profile. A 2.91 AST/TO ratio puts him among the most efficient playmakers in the draft. The defensive potential on top of this makes him genuinely special.

players.name: Mikel Brown Jr.
players.verdict: Clear runway in Brooklyn. A spectacular live-dribble passer and versatile creator with an improved burst and first step - dribble, pass, shoot at an elite level when healthy. Draws fouls at high volume. Nursed a lower back injury through the college season, otherwise he would likely be in the top 5.

players.name: Keaton Wagler
players.verdict: Came out of nowhere as a freshman at Illinois and goes at Pick 5 to the Clippers to take up the reins next to Darius Garland. An exceptional shooter and processor who thrives in movement. The dynasty case is built on shooting creation. Reminds me of Haliburton.

players.name: Darius Acuff Jr.
players.verdict: Sacremento have themselves their new franchise PG of the future. Elite PTS, elite AST and elite 3PM on high volume. A 2.97 AST/TO ratio and arguably the most efficient high-volume playmaker in the class. He will bring you elite guard statistics right from the get go which is why he rises on my board.

players.name: Brayden Burries
players.verdict: Burries had a lot of buzz leading up to the draft and lands in a new-look Bucks lineup with Giannis shipped off to MIA. A reliable, dependable guard, that should develop into the ideal third option who brings depth and ball-handling stability to any backcourt. Consistent multi-contributor floor.

players.name: Allen Graves
players.verdict: The most elite steal rate in the class, showing his hunting abilities off in summer league. A chaos creator with phenomenal feel, so he slots into the Raptors culture nicely - exceptional on the offensive glass with the size and physicality to impact every possession. Historic multi-cat defensive production for a wing. The one caveat is Santa Clara is not a Power 6 programme.

players.name: Morez Johnson Jr.
players.verdict: Drafted higher than expected by his former Michigan coach, now at the helm in Dallas. This is a great sign for his value. An explosive athlete with high-level rim protection and interior defense. One of the premier frontcourt defensive prospects in this rookie class.

players.name: Yaxel Lendeborg
players.verdict: A rare shooting profile for a forward of his size. A sizable wing who excels in transition with high-level shooting and passing. A genuine multi-tool forward. Age 24 is the only reason not to draft him in the top 10. Expect him to slot into Kerr's rotation and generate fantasy value from the get go. Has the potential to be the best rookie in year 1 outside Boozer.

players.name: Hannes Steinbach
players.verdict: Elite REB and elite FG% on volume in college - drafted by CHA who will have a new look roster in 2026-27. Best rebounder in the class minute-for-minute. A strong, physical frontcourt presence who brings interior balance and positional strength that complements more rangy lineups.

players.name: Ebuka Okorie
players.verdict: One of our guys that we've been higher than consensus throughout. Good sign withs DET trading up to get him in the top 20. The Pistons struggled in the playoffs to generate offence outside of Cade Cunningham, so the opportunity will be there early for playing time. Gets to the basket more than any guard in the class. Absolutely electric with the best first step in the draft - pure scoring gravity and draws fouls at high volume which is the strongest indicator the scoring translates to NBA level.

players.name: Aday Mara
players.verdict: Was one of guys throughout the college season before he emerged in March Madness. Unfortunately landing at OKC suppresses the immediate value, but the long-value should not be overlooked. The most elite shot-blocker in the entire 2026 class by a distance. A true needle-mover at center position for your dynasty team. The interior presence and rim protection profile is rare at this age. Very good passer for a big man.

players.name: Cameron Carr
players.verdict: Fantastic in summer league. A class-leading shooting volume profile. An athletic movement shooter who is also an exceptional shot-blocker for a wing. A rare combination of spacing and defensive versatility. NBA translation thesis is built on shooting and shot-blocking.

players.name: Labaron Philon
players.verdict: Scored at will in summer league on low efficiency. One of the most underrated scoring profiles in the class. A shifty primary creator with elite rim pressure and trustworthy defensive upside - breaks down defenses off the dribble as well as anyone in this class. He recently said in an interview that Alpy Sengun will be the first superstar whose ankles he breaks!

players.name: Meleek Thomas
players.verdict: Some are calling him a modern day Jamal Crawford after he balled out in summer league. Averaged 28 PTS on 50% FG and 46% from 3PA. An excellent complementary player with a unique shotmaking touch. Outstanding off-ball defense, movement skills and an innate ability to jump passing lanes.

players.name: Christian Anderson
players.verdict: The big riser due to the LaMelo Ball trade! The most prolific assist creator in the class and arguably its best shooter and elite pull-up ability and pick-and-roll craft that few guards in this draft can match. Specialist profile who has landed in a dream spot. Don't fade!

players.name: Bennett Stirtz
players.verdict: A crafty creator with pull-up shooting and real scoring juice off the dribble - alleviates pressure from primary initiators in a way that doesn't always show in the stat line. Older prospect at age 23 compresses the dynasty runway but he can slot into OKC and help them straight away and the category stat set is real if he hits.

players.name: Dailyn Swain
players.verdict: Drafted to Chicago - another guy with a class-leading defensive steal rate. A lengthy wing who brings essential creation against tough, athletic defenses - the size and secondary playmaking are the dynasty calling cards. SEC Newcomer of the Year. At 20 years old the development runway is there.

players.name: Sergio De Larrea
players.verdict: Taken by DAL earlier than some thought. Has to battle with Ryan Nembhard for playing time. A creative, high-feel playmaker out of Valencia whose passing vision and court sense are the standout traits. The scoring and size are limited. A specialist point guard whose dynasty value lives and dies with assist volume and whether he earns NBA minutes.

players.name: Zuby Ejiofor
players.verdict: Solid in summer league and expect him to break into ATL's rotation immediately. A versatile big who brings utility as a handler and passer - had some huge lines with St Johns and has shown constant improvement at every level. Draws fouls at high volume. Has the potential to outperform this slot.

players.name: Nate Ament
players.verdict: A gigantic wing with undeniable shotmaking off movement. The strength and physicality to impose himself have improved significantly. Draws fouls at high volume. The scoring has room to grow if the shot diet evolves at NBA level. A development play.

players.name: Ryan Conwell
players.verdict: Strong summer league showing. One of the highest three-point volumes in the country at nearly 10 attempts per game, paired with a reliable 83% from the line. A pure movement shooter who lives at the rim and beyond the arc, almost never settling for long twos. The shooting gravity and free-throw efficiency are the dynasty anchors. A specialist whose one elite skill is the most portable in the modern game.

players.name: Bruce Thornton
players.verdict: A steady, high-IQ guard with scoring punch and playmaking vision wo pooped in summer league. The type of backcourt piece who keeps the stat sheet balanced across multiple categories. No single elite anchor but the consistency and floor are real. Age and shooting development will determine the dynasty ceiling.

players.name: Tarris Reed Jr.
players.verdict: Elite REB, elite BLK and elite FG% at 60.7%. A traditional center who imposes a physical edge and brings size and strength that impacts every possession. NCAA Tournament East Region MOP: 19.5 PPG and 13.2 RPG over 6 games. Older prospect at age 23. Could he be the Walker Kessler of this class?

players.name: Joshua Jefferson
players.verdict: A 6'8", 246-pound point-forward with elite passing, a high basketball IQ and multi-positional defense. The only player in Big 12 history to post 450+ points, 250+ rebounds, 100+ assists, 70+ steals and 25+ blocks in a season. A Denzel Valentine-style stat-stuffer whose all-around production fills every column on the sheet. Few forwards in this class carry this many categories.

players.name: Koa Peat
players.verdict: A physical presence with real strength and rebounding. Shows flashes of mid-range touch and the ability to impact games through interior physicality. A physicality-and-scoring development play.

players.name: Jayden Quaintance
players.verdict: Elite BLK's a genuine category anchor from scouting context. A slasher, play finisher and secondary passer with massive defensive potential. Only 4 games played due to injury. Ratings from scouting and prior college season stats. The upside is there. Expected to sit out 2026-27 season with a long-term injury, so he becomes a deeper league stash only.

players.name: Emanuel Sharp
players.verdict: Sacramento keeps finding guys who fit their rebuild culture and Sharp checks every one of those boxes. He is a 3-and-D wing who brings off-ball shooting and defensive effort that modern teams pay for. Everything hinges on whether his shooting efficiency translates to the NBA level, but if it does, this could quietly be one of the late-round steals of the class.

players.name: Karim Lopez
players.verdict: NBL Next Stars pathway. Aame programme that produced LaMelo Ball, Josh Giddey and Alex Sarr. A developmental wing with improved shooting and solid ball skills. The physical strength and athleticism for a versatile two-way role are already visible. 6'9" with 7'1" wingspan. Youngest wing in the class at 19.0. Pure ceiling bet.

players.name: Trevon Brazile
players.verdict: A rare dual-defensive anchor at 6'10" with near-7'4" wingspan and a 41" max vertical. The athletic ceiling is massive and the defensive rebound rate confirms the motor is real. A growing divide exists on whether the ball skills can catch up to the raw physical gifts. The defensive production is not a projection, it's already there.

players.name: Chris Cenac Jr
players.verdict: Led Houston in rebounding as a freshman, the first to do so since 2011-12, with a career-high 18-board NCAA Tournament game. A mobile 6'11" big with a 7'4" wingspan who finishes as a lob and roll threat and has flashed three-point range. The youngest player in this tier and the only true freshman. The rebounding floor and developing shooting touch give him the longest dynasty runway of the group.

players.name: Henri Veesaar
players.verdict: Fell in the draft as Atlanta made him a promise for a guaranteed deal, so don't be too alarmed. Elite FG% at 60.8%. A 7'0" stretch big who shot 43% from three on nearly 100 attempts and posted 13 double-doubles. A skilled, mobile center with a soft shooting touch from mid-range and beyond the arc. Fits the inside-out template every roster is hunting for. The shooting at his size is the dynasty calling card.

players.name: Richie Saunders
players.verdict: A hyper-efficient role player with a relentless motor and high-percentage perimeter shooting that translates to any system. The defensive activity and shooting consistency are exactly what contending rosters need. Age 25 compresses the dynasty runway and he will sit out most of the 2025-26 with a torn right ACL.

players.name: Dillon Mitchell
players.verdict: Elite FG% - finishes everything at the rim and almost never settles for jumpers. A relentless motor on the glass and a surprisingly gifted connective passer for a forward, with an assist-to-turnover ratio that ranked top-15 nationally. The rebounding, steals and efficiency travel. A glue-guy profile that wins category weeks without needing the ball.

players.name: Isaiah Evans
players.verdict: A tough, physical movement shooter whose grit and competitiveness stand out on tape. Shoots more threes per minute than anyone in the class. The dynasty floor rises and falls with three-point shooting.

players.name: Baba Miller
players.verdict: A 6'10" forward with a 7'1" wingspan and a wing-like skill set in a big man's body. Fluid ball-handling and elite recovery speed have scouts pushing him well into the first round. The physical tools and defensive versatility are rare at his size. The production hasn't matched the physical profile yet. A ceiling play built on the belief that ball skills catch up to the frame.

players.name: Ja'Kobi Gillespie
players.verdict: Set Tennessee's single-season steals record (79) and became the first player in SEC history with 200 assists and 100 made threes in a season. A microwave lead guard with deep range and quick hands, the rare profile that anchors both the assist and steal columns while chipping in triples and free-throw percentage. Size is the NBA question; the category production is not.

players.name: Braden Smith
players.verdict: Purdue's floor general. One of the most complete point guard profiles in the class. Anchors three columns while shooting efficiently from deep. The scoring and rebounding are limited by size but the playmaking, defensive activity and shooting translate at any level.

players.name: Alex Karaban
players.verdict: A 6'8" forward who stretches the floor from every spot and converts at the line at an elite rate. The shooting translates immediately. Age 23.2 compresses the dynasty runway - the production is ready-made, the timeline is short.

players.name: Izaiyah Nelson
players.verdict: Orlando landing Nelson is a genuinely good fit. He is compact for a big man but compensates with terrific length, physicality, and an elite motor that never shuts off. His defensive instincts play well above his draft position, and the Magic have the patience to let his offensive game develop over time. A strong late-round flier in dynasty leagues.

players.name: Tyler Bilodeau
players.verdict: Bilodeau is a scorer with an interesting offensive mix, able to shoot from deep, finish at the rim, and lean on some old-school post game. The athleticism and defensive limitations are real concerns that landed him on a two-way deal, but he gets runway to develop in Brooklyn. The scoring is worth keeping tabs on.

players.name: Quadir Copeland
players.verdict: Led the ACC in assists at 6.5 per game. Set a career high of 16 assists in one game. The passing, defensive activity and shooting combine in a way that makes him a stashable two-way option in deep leagues.

players.name: Bryce Hopkins
players.verdict: At summer league he caught my eye and moves up our board. Averaged 18 pts 6 reb on high efficiency.

players.name: Nick Martinelli
players.verdict: A back-to-back Big Ten scoring champion who shot 42% from three - a left-handed forward with elite footwork, mismatch-hunting ability in the post and genuine physicality. The scoring touch and shooting efficiency are the dynasty calling cards. A major value grab at this range whose offensive skill set is more polished than most forwards ranked above him.

players.name: Jack Kayil
players.verdict: A playmaking guard who led Germany to a FIBA U19 silver medal with 6.6 APG and earned BBL Best Young Player honors at 20 years old against professionals nearly a decade his senior. The passing and ball skills are genuine. FG% and 3PM are the severe category drags - 40% from the field and 34% from deep need significant improvement at NBA level. A development play built on playmaking upside and age. He's staying in Europe, so a stash in deeper leagues.

players.name: Tyler Nickel
players.verdict: A highly efficient 3PT specialist who averaged 3 3PM in summer league. Could help you in 3s in deeper leagues

players.name: Maliq Brown
players.verdict: Brown is one of the purest defensive prospects in the class with elite motor, IQ, and intensity on that end of the floor. The problem is the offensive game is essentially nonexistent, which makes a sustainable NBA role hard to project. If any organization can find a way to use a player like this, it is San Antonio. Worth boarding as a deep dynasty flier in leagues that reward defensive counting stats.

players.name: Felix Okpara
players.verdict: Okpara projects as a low-maintenance, high-energy backup center. Because Washington's frontcourt features established depth, his two-way contract gives the Wizards a no-risk player they can steadily develop in the G League.

players.name: Tobe Awaka
players.verdict: Chicago under Bryson Graham wants players who compete, rebound, and bring energy every single night, and Awaka embodies exactly that. He is an explosive, physical presence who attacks the glass relentlessly and never takes a possession off. The limitation is real: at 6-8, he needs to live below the rim, and the offensive arsenal is thin. He will need to carve a niche as an elite energy and rebounding specialist, but the two-way deal is a legitimate foothold.

players.name: Ugonna Onyenso
players.verdict: A true rim protector whose shot-blocking rate is among the best in the class. The defensive impact anchors the entire profile. Offensively limited - the scoring and shooting will not carry dynasty value. A defensive specialist who's lack of offensive capabilities are concerning.

players.name: Jaylin Sellers
players.verdict: Sellers projects as a highly efficient "3-and-D" depth piece or microwave bench scorer. His immediate pathways to minutes in Chicago rely on his lethal spot-up shooting, allowing him to cleanly slot into modern NBA spacing frameworks. Likely spends most of his time in the G-league.

players.name: Otega Oweh
players.verdict: Oweh has a chance to develop into a Lu Dort style stopper, so fitting that the Thunder drafted him. Don't expect him to feature much in year 1 given OKC's depth.

players.name: Jaden Bradley
players.verdict: A crafty, pass-first guard with active hands and defensive disruption - the playmaking instincts and steal creation are the dynasty calling cards. The shooting needs significant development before the full multi-category profile unlocks. A high-floor, moderate-ceiling prospect.

players.name: Tobi Lawal
players.verdict: Lawal is a good athlete with loads of flair, but his game is more relevant to era's gone by. No outside shot but has potential as a plug-and-play energy guy.

players.name: Tre Donaldson
players.verdict: Donaldson fits the precise mold of an unheralded, gritty guard that the Heat organization historically excels at transforming into a rotation asset. He could surprise with potential opportunities to showcase his point-of-attack defense and floor general traits.

players.name: Jaron Pierre Jr.
players.verdict: Jaron Pierre Jr. profiles as a points and three-point volume streamer. If injuries force him into the rotation, he will easily buoy your scoring columns, but his limited historical defensive event generation caps his floor.

players.name: Rafael Castro
players.verdict: Elite REB and elite FG% - two genuine category anchors. A physical, imposing center who dominates the glass and finishes at an elite rate around the rim. A non-shooter - the 3PM is absent. The dynasty case is built entirely on rebounding and efficiency as a traditional interior big. Two-way deal with the young Bucks is intriguing.

players.name: Nate Bittle
players.verdict: Bittle going undrafted despite a 7-foot frame and 7-5 wingspan almost certainly signals medical concerns worth factoring into any investment. That said, the offensive tools for a big of his size are genuinely uncommon, and he scores with touch and moves reasonably well for the position. Toronto gives him an Exhibit-10 opportunity, and if the medicals prove manageable, he is an underrated upside swing.

players.name: Nick Boyd
players.verdict: Boyd is a sharp shotmaker with genuine ball-handling and playmaking ability, but his frame will be the persistent question at the NBA level. Golden State giving him an Exhibit-10 is a meaningful endorsement. Summer League will be his proving ground, and the offensive tools are legitimate. This is purely a defense-and-size bet at this stage.

players.name: Duke Miles
players.verdict: A well-rounded international guard whose passing and defensive activity stand out - the profile contributes across multiple categories without a glaring weakness. Exhibit 10 with PHI gives him some hope to work it out. Keep an eye out.

players.name: Aaron Nkrumah
players.verdict: Draft boards had Nkrumah pegged as a second-rounder but he slipped all the way through undrafted, a genuine surprise given the tools. At 6-6 with a 6-10 wingspan, excellent defensive instincts, and a well-rounded fantasy profile with positive shooting indicators, the upside is real. Denver gives him an Exhibit-10 shot to prove it. Worth a stash in deeper dynasty formats.

players.name: Darrion Williams
players.verdict: A versatile, productive wing whose value comes from contributing across multiple categories without a glaring weakness. Scoring, shooting and free-throw efficiency all register. No single elite anchor but the balanced profile plays in every format. A steady, low-variance contributor.

players.name: Peter Suder
players.verdict: Suder scores a two-way with the Lakers. Has a lot of flash and connective skills that gives me some hope. A potential plug-and-play rotation player outcome here if it hits.
